questions.prompt: Why are tenant and group fields absent from AskPayload?
options: Pydantic cannot validate sets
Identity and authorization scope must come from authenticated application state
They would make the payload too large
The generator should infer them from the question
questions.explanation: Schema-valid caller input is still caller-controlled. Authentication middleware or another trusted application boundary must establish identity and scope.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest reason to authorize documents before ranking?
options: It always improves semantic relevance
It makes embeddings deterministic
Unauthorized material can otherwise leak through scores, timing, caches, logs, or context
It removes the need for tenant IDs
questions.explanation: Late filtering may protect the final list but still expose unauthorized material to ranking and downstream side channels.

questions.prompt: A generator returns a schema-valid citation ID that was not retrieved. What should happen?
options: Accept it because the schema is valid
Ask the generator whether it is confident
Reject it against the trusted authorized evidence set
Log it and return the answer
questions.explanation: Typed structure does not establish provenance or authorization. The trusted application verifies evidence IDs.

questions.prompt: Which design best enforces a five-second user-visible SLA across retrieval and generation?
options: Give each dependency a five-second timeout
Use one end-to-end deadline and allocate/propagate the remaining budget
Retry every exception until one call succeeds
Run both stages in background tasks after returning success
questions.explanation: Independent full-length timeouts can exceed the total SLA. The operation needs a shared deadline and cancellation.

questions.prompt: What does the deterministic generator primarily enable?
options: Proof that production model quality is high
Fast repeatable tests of orchestration and policy invariants
Removal of all live-model evaluation
Automatic authorization of generated citations
questions.explanation: A mock isolates software behavior. It cannot measure a live model's quality, robustness, safety, or latency.

questions.prompt: Which denominator best supports cost per successful compliant task?
options: All requests
Only successful answers, including policy violations
Successful answers whose citations remain within authorized evidence
Only refused requests
questions.explanation: The numerator should include all work, while the denominator counts outcomes that both succeed and satisfy the compliance invariant.

questions.prompt: When is a Retriever Protocol most justified?
options: For every one-line helper
When it protects a meaningful provider/data boundary and improves independent testing
Only when using FastAPI dependency injection
When the concrete retriever can never change
questions.explanation: Ports have carrying cost. They earn it at meaningful volatility, trust, and test boundaries.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between pyproject.toml and an application lockfile?
options: Both should contain only exact pins
The manifest declares acceptable requirements; the lock records a tested resolution
The lock replaces project metadata
The manifest records every transitive package from pip freeze
questions.explanation: The manifest expresses direct dependencies and compatibility; the application lock makes a concrete environment reproducible.

questions.prompt: Which failure is normally terminal rather than retryable?
options: A transient network reset before any effect
A provider 503 within remaining budget
An authorization denial
A rate limit with a short Retry-After
questions.explanation: Retrying cannot turn a policy denial into authorization and may become an evasion attempt.

questions.prompt: Which telemetry is most appropriate for this service?
options: Full prompts, documents, credentials, and hidden reasoning
Only a final success boolean
Request IDs, evidence IDs, policy reason codes, versions, budgets, latency, and terminal state
No telemetry because AI content may be sensitive
questions.explanation: Operationally useful metadata can be captured while minimizing sensitive content and excluding secrets/private reasoning.
